levels.label: א
levels.name: Alef
levels.guidance: Write for an end-of-Alef learner who can decode unpointed Hebrew. Prefer very common concrete words, active clauses, familiar verb forms, and one event or thought per short sentence. Avoid passive or nominal phrasing, formal connectors, unnecessary foreign terms, dense construct chains, and nested clauses. Explain a necessary less-common term immediately in simple words. Keep the voice adult and natural. Difficulty is determined by wording and sentence shape, not word count.

levels.label: א+
levels.name: Alef Plus
levels.guidance: Write for advanced Alef. Use a broader but still common vocabulary than Alef, past and future forms where natural, simple cause and effect, everyday connectors, common fixed expressions, and occasional short subordinate clauses. Keep the story easy to follow. Difficulty is determined by wording and grammar, not word count.

levels.label: ב
levels.name: Bet
levels.guidance: Write reasonably natural contemporary Hebrew for a Bet learner. Use a wider everyday vocabulary, more precise verbs and adjectives, natural connectors, comparisons, reactions, common colloquial constructions, and moderately more complex sentences than Alef Plus. Avoid dense journalistic syntax and specialist vocabulary. Difficulty is determined by wording and grammar, not word count.
